name: NROL-136
destination_explanation: Most of the satellites working today are down here, which has made this by far the most crowded stretch of space around the planet.
slot_a_text: Fifteenth batch of satellites for a reconnaissance satellite constellation built by SpaceX and Northrop Grumman for the National Reconnaissance Office to provide imaging and other reconnaissance capabilities.
slot_b_text: Low Earth orbit is anywhere from about 160 to 2,000 km up, where a satellite laps the planet roughly every 90 minutes. Everything there is falling; it just keeps missing the ground.

lg_slot_b_text: This is the 14th flight for B1097. It flew itself back to Landing Zone 4. It last flew USSF-259 about 2 months ago.
lg_slot_c_text: That is 72 launches from SLC-4E this year, out of 310 since its first in 1964. Its previous launch was only a day earlier.
